articles.title: Zelensky rejects wartime elections, saying vote would 'split' Ukraine
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said that holding elections during wartime would pose a threat to the country, following a controversial call by his former defense minister to pave the way for an election. According to the latest opinion poll by the Kyiv Institute of Sociology carried out this summer, only 15 per cent of those surveyed want an election to be held at this time. Details by Eliza Herbert.

articles.title: Zelensky rejects rival's call for elections, says would be 'huge risk' for Ukraine
articles.description: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has rejected the prospect of wartime elections, saying it would be highly dangerous. The remarks come in response to a call from the former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov to organise a vote, after he was fired by Zelensky last month. Analysis by FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Matthew-Mary Caruchet.

articles.title: How will European politicians react to a summer of extreme heat?
articles.description: Europe this summer has had to face record breaking temperatures, which caused droughts, deaths, and caused devastating wildfires. While the latest heat dome has dissipated, the damage remains – the continent continues to be the fastest warming globally. Will this summer serve as a global climate reckoning? articles.title: Thousands rally in Sweden to protest climate policies ahead of general election
articles.description: Some 10,000 people rallied in Stockholm on Sunday to demand stronger action on climate change, weeks before Sweden’s general election. Climate campaigner Greta Thunberg joined the rally, as organisers accused the government of weakening emissions policies and urged politicians to act faster to meet Sweden’s climate targets.

articles.title: French holidaymakers head north to enjoy cooler destinations
articles.description: The summer holidays in France are continuing. However, as we head towards the end of August, a trend has emerged. Destinations in the north of the country are proving more popular, due to the series of heatwaves the country has experienced this year.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia asserts its dominance over Esports as MBS arrives in Paris for 'World Cup'
articles.description: Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman arrives in France for a two-day visit this Sunday. President Emmanuel Macron is hosting the crown prince for the closing ceremony of the so-called Esports World Cup in Paris… which is organised and financed by the Saudis. Analysis by Andy Miah, chair of Sciences Communication & Future Media at the University of Salford.

articles.title: Presidential campaign heats up in Brazil, as Lula and F. Bolsonaro hold rival rallies
articles.description: Brazilian president Lula de Silva and his political opponent Flavio Bolsonaro pressed on with their presidential campaigns over the weekend, as both candidates held rallies in Rio De Janeiro. Top of the agenda for both candidates was crime, though the two took distinctly different approaches to the issue. Details by Camille Corcoran.

articles.title: Hundreds of Gaza children join a mass swimming lesson to cope with trauma
articles.description: In Gaza, the war has upended the lives of an entire generation of children. In an effort to help them cope with the trauma of the conflict, an NGO has launched a project in Khan Younis: a huge swimming lesson that could even set a world record. Hundreds of children have gathered on the beach to learn how to swim. Story by Charlotte Hughes.

articles.title: Venezuela: Two months after the quake, 12,500 people still live in temporary camps
articles.description: Two months after two earthquakes struck Venezuela, more than 12,500 people are still living in temporary camps in La Guaira. Many survivors are still struggling to come to terms with the loss of loved ones and their homes. They have been forced to adapt to precarious living conditions, exposed to the elements, with little access to medical care and humanitarian aid. France 24 reporters Herminia Fernández and Julio Uribarris visited three camps housing earthquake survivors.

articles.title: Middle East live: Israeli strikes kill three, including child, in Gaza Strip
articles.description: Israeli strikes in the central Gaza Strip killed three people, including a child, on Sunday, according to rescuers. The strikes came two days after a Palestinian teenager was killed by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank following a rock-throwing incident. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

articles.title: South Korea tests Arctic route with a first container shipped to Europe
articles.description: Reaching Europe from Asia via the Arctic is nothing new... Russia and China have used this route for years. But yesterday, South Korea sent its first container ship along this path to avoid the traffic blockade in the Middle East. Experts warn the shift could further accelerate the melting of polar ice.

articles.title: US-Canada trade dispute escalates after Carney announces retaliatory tariffs
articles.description: Canada and the US were closing in on a trade deal earlier this week until the negotiations fell apart. Both sides blame each other for last-minute changes to the terms. Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney has announced retaliatory tariffs on the United States after Washington imposed a 50 percent levy on 20-billion-dollars worth of Canadian goods. On Saturday, he addressed the nation for the first time since the talks collapsed, as Charlotte Lam explains.

articles.title: Iran escalates threats as US pushes economic isolation
articles.description: Tensions between Iran and the United States continue to escalate. Tehran is threatening to regard as enemies any countries that join the US sanctions, in response to Washington’s calls to isolate its economy. A press conference is scheduled for Monday to outline the US strategy. Story by Camille Corcoran.

articles.title: L’Assurance-maladie reconnaît officiellement le «syndrome de fatigue chronique»
articles.description: Il y a quelques jours, le site Ameli.fr a discrètement modifié la fiche consacrée à cette maladie, retirant les mentions relatives à un «trouble psychiatrique ou psychologique». Les associations de malades saluent cette avancée.

articles.title: Macron hosts Saudi crown prince for two-day visit to include issues from energy to Mideast

articles.title: China abruptly delays ambitious Chang’e-7 mission to find water ice on moon

articles.title: Les Etats-Unis mettent en garde le Canada contre les effets "dévastateurs" d'un conflit commercial
